title: Runlevels and systemd targets
subtitle: Machine state after boot — SysV runlevels mapped to systemd

cards.meaning: State of the machine after boot: which services are on, networking, GUI, or shutting down
cards.notes: Classic SysV: the system is in one runlevel at a time.

cards.meaning: Halt / power off
cards.notes: Memory hook: 0 = zero life (halt).

cards.meaning: Single-user / rescue-style maintenance — usually no network services
cards.notes: Memory hook: 1 = lonely admin. Lower levels for maintenance/emergency.

cards.meaning: Multi-user, text, networking — typical server
cards.notes: Memory hook: 3 = server. Emulated by multi-user.target.

cards.meaning: Often unused / custom; some distros treat it like 3
cards.notes: Default runlevels are typically 3, 4, or 5.

cards.meaning: Multi-user with graphical desktop
cards.notes: Memory hook: 5 = GUI. Emulated by graphical.target.

cards.meaning: Reboot
cards.notes: Memory hook: 6 = full circle (reboot).

cards.meaning: Usually 3, 4, or 5
cards.notes: Lower runlevels are for maintenance because they usually offer no network services.

cards.meaning: Per-runlevel start/stop scripts (symlinks)
cards.notes: Symlinks into ../init.d/ with K/S prefixes.

cards.meaning: Kill (stop) nfs at this runlevel; 20 is the order
cards.notes: K = Kill. Lower number runs first.

cards.meaning: Start network at this runlevel; 10 is the order
cards.notes: S = Start. Lower number runs first.

cards.meaning: Classic SysV file for default runlevel
cards.notes: Example boots into runlevel 3.

cards.meaning: systemd uses targets, not runlevels; old runlevel names exist as compatibility symlinks
cards.notes: Know the mapping 0→poweroff, 1→rescue, 3→multi-user, 5→graphical, 6→reboot.

cards.meaning: systemd target for halt/power off (old runlevel 0)
cards.notes: Compatibility symlink: runlevel0.target.

cards.meaning: systemd target for single-user/rescue (old runlevel 1)
cards.notes: Compatibility symlink: runlevel1.target.

cards.meaning: Network + text, no GUI — emulates runlevel 3
cards.notes: Compatibility symlink: runlevel3.target. Typical server default.

cards.meaning: Multi-user with GUI — emulates runlevel 5
cards.notes: Compatibility symlink: runlevel5.target.

cards.meaning: systemd target for reboot (old runlevel 6)
cards.notes: Compatibility symlink: runlevel6.target.

cards.meaning: Even more minimal than rescue — its own target, not a classic numbered runlevel
cards.notes: No runlevelN.target compatibility entry in the course table.

cards.meaning: Show which target the machine boots into
cards.notes: View the default target.

cards.meaning: Set default boot target to server (text + network, no GUI)
cards.notes: Safer everyday example from the notes.

cards.meaning: Set default boot target to desktop GUI
cards.notes: Safer everyday example from the notes.

cards.notes: Example from the notes showing a dangerous default.

cards.notes: Immediate switch; get-default/set-default control what you boot into.
